title: Uways al-Qarani
hookLine: a man from Yemen who never met the Prophet ﷺ, cared for his mother, and whose prayers were sought
tomorrow: The women who asked for a day

cards: Every time a fresh group of fighters arrives in Medina from Yemen, Umar ibn al-Khattab goes out to meet them with the same question. Is Uways ibn Amir among you? Again and again, no.
Umar leads the whole community by now, and still he keeps asking after one man he has never seen. Then one day a voice in the crowd says yes. Umar walks up to him and asks his own favor: pray for me.

teach.b: The story is in Sahih Muslim, and Umar tells us why he kept asking.
He had heard the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, describe a man who would come with the reinforcements from Yemen: Uways ibn Amir, of the tribe of Murad, then of the clan of Qaran.
He had suffered a skin disease and been cured of it, except for one small patch.
And he had a mother, and he was devoted to her. Then something remarkable: if this man swore by God, God would make his oath come true. If you meet him, ask him to seek forgiveness for you.
So Umar checks every detail, and Uways confirms them all: Murad, Qaran, the healed skin, the mother.
Then Umar, the companion of the Prophet, asks a man who never met the Prophet to pray for him. And Uways does. Why did he never meet him?
The hadith only says he was dutiful to his mother. Tradition says that is exactly what kept him in Yemen: she needed him, and he stayed. That link is the tradition's, not the hadith's words.
Then the end of the conversation. Umar asks where he is going. Kufa, says Uways.
Umar offers to write to the governor there for him, and Uways declines. He would rather be among the ordinary people, the ones nobody notices.
He had a recommendation from the leader of the believers in his hand, and he let it go. The man whose prayer was sought was the man who did not seek to be seen.
And in the Prophet's description, the one deed named is not a battle or a speech.
It is his care for his mother.

how: Muslims retell the report in Sahih Muslim of Umar seeking out Uways and asking for his prayer, and often hold him up as an example of devotion to a parent and of a hidden, humble life.

o: a companion who fought beside the Prophet at Badr
a man of Yemen, devoted to his mother, whose prayer Umar sought
a governor of Kufa appointed by Umar ibn al-Khattab

p: asked every group from Yemen about him
ask him to seek forgiveness for you
where Uways said he was going

s: Uways was a close companion who sat with the Prophet in Medina
he never met the Prophet. the Prophet described him, and Umar found him later.
Uways turned down Umar's offer to write to the governor
he said he would rather be among the ordinary people.
the hadith in Muslim says outright that his mother kept him from traveling
Muslim says he was devoted to his mother. that this kept him in Yemen is the tradition's telling.

games.q: you're Uways. Umar, leader of the believers, offers to write a letter to the governor of Kufa for you. what do you do?
o: take the letter and go straight to the governor.
thank him and decline: you'd rather be among ordinary people.
ask for a post in Medina instead.
games.why: Muslim reports he declined, preferring to be among the ordinary people. the man whose prayer was sought didn't seek to be seen.

practice: Bring to mind your mother or father, or whoever raised you, and one ordinary thing they need right now: a call, a ride, a meal, ten minutes of listening without your phone.
If your parent has died, hold them in mind instead and, if you pray, ask mercy for them. If the relationship is hard, choose something small and safe, or simply wish them well.

wordCard.voice: Uways al-Qarani. A man of Qaran in Yemen, devoted to his mother, described by the Prophet, and sought out by Umar for his prayer. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Uways, of the clan of Qaran.

carryVoice: Your line: he stayed with his mother. Unseen, and still sought out. That's day eight hundred fifty-seven.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2542 (the Prophet describes Uways; Umar seeks him from the Yemeni reinforcements; Uways declines the letter to Kufa)
